newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude trades completing April business.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude trades completing April business.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices held slightly firmer for outrights, while domestic grades continued to falter on the last day for completing April business ahead of pipeline scheduling.

"It looks like most people are just about done with April," said a crude broker. The April/May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing spread had been reduced to flat against the benchmark, but recovered lately to around 10-13 cents over the mark, traders said.
April WTI stood at $21.25-35 a barrel, compared with the May WTI cash price of $21.15-25, 10 cts higher than on Monday.
Grade trading featured April Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James selling at a 55 and 60 cts discount to the marker in what traders said were desperation plays.
"It looks like a freak thing to get done that weak," said one trader, noting the economics of buying at the price were prohibitive, and not likely bought by a refiner.
Sweet domestic barrels are battling against weak North Sea Brent prices, where the latest wet deal was done at 90 cts under the May Brent paper level on Tuesday for Mar 31-Apr 2.
Other deals were scarce, with May WTI/Cushing Postings moving at $1.78, West Texas Sour/Midland at -$2.45 and the Apr/May roll at +13 cts.
Outright crude traders trained attention on tonight's American Petroleum Institute (API) stock report, pushing aside the unrest in Nigeria for the moment.
Protesting villagers have taken Royal Dutch/Shell Group workers hostage, but the extent of supply disruptions have not yet shaken the market, traders said.
The Reuters API survey saw crude building by an average of 1.75 million barrels, distillates declining 2.25 million barrels and gasoline stocks drawing 1.25 million barrels.
